Published 3 hours ago on October 24, 2026 By Kulu Media News Desk US President Donald Trump appears in an ABC News video report about his remarks on a possible new military operation against Iran. Image credit: ABC News / Screenshot by Kulu Media US President Donald Trump has raised the possibility of another military operation against Iran, warning that Washington could resume strikes as efforts to reach a settlement to the nearly eight-month conflict remain unresolved. Speaking at a political rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on Friday, October 23, 2026, Trump referred to the US military campaign known as Operation Epic Fury while discussing the possibility of further action against Tehran. “We may do another little Epic Fury,” Trump said, according to Reuters . The president did not provide details about potential targets, the timing of another operation or whether any military action had been authorized. His remarks come amid continuing diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, which began with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Trump Raises Prospect of Renewed Military Action During the Florida rally, Trump referred to previous American military operations against Iran, including Operation Midnight Hammer and Operation Epic Fury. According to Anadolu Agency , Trump suggested that Tehran could face another military operation if negotiations failed to produce an agreement. He also claimed that earlier US strikes had severely damaged Iran’s nuclear enrichment capabilities. Those assertions reflect the president’s assessment of the military campaign and do not establish that Iran’s nuclear capabilities have been completely eliminated. The remarks add to uncertainty about Washington’s next steps as the administration weighs further military pressure against diplomatic efforts to resolve the conflict. The United States and Israel launched their initial military campaign against Iran on February 28, targeting Iranian military and nuclear-related facilities. The opening strikes and Iran’s subsequent retaliation were covered in Kulu Media’s earlier report on the US-Israel strikes . Since then, the conflict has expanded into a prolonged confrontation affecting regional security, international energy markets and commercial shipping. Earlier Promise to Avoid Strikes Before US Elections Trump’s latest remarks follow an earlier statement that the United States would not launch new attacks against Iran before the November 3 congressional midterm elections. On October 8, the president said Washington was engaged in productive discussions with Tehran and would refrain from further strikes before the vote. That position was documented in a separate Reuters report . The president did not explicitly withdraw that commitment during Friday’s rally, leaving the potential timing of any renewed military action unclear. Earlier on October 23, Trump also told reporters that the United States could bring the war to an end quickly but questioned whether Washington should pursue an immediate conclusion or allow the confrontation to diminish gradually. His statements indicate that the administration continues to consider different approaches to the conflict without announcing a final military or diplomatic decision. Iran War Continues to Affect Global Energy Markets The possibility of renewed strikes comes as the conflict continues to affect international energy supplies and shipping routes. The Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, remains a major concern because of its importance to global oil and gas transportation. Military tensions and uncertainty surrounding shipping through the waterway have contributed to higher energy prices and increased market volatility. Kulu Media previously examined the economic consequences in its report on European stocks , as international oil prices climbed above $110 per barrel. Higher energy costs have placed additional pressure on businesses and consumers, including in countries that depend heavily on imported petroleum products. The conflict has also affected maritime security beyond the Persian Gulf, particularly around the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Continued fighting involving Yemen’s Houthi movement has raised concerns about commercial shipping and energy infrastructure along the Arabian Peninsula. Earlier this month, a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport caused substantial casualties and disrupted aviation operations in Saudi Arabia. Although the Saudi-Houthi confrontation has its own military and political dynamics, instability across these interconnected waterways has increased concerns about regional security. Possible Implications for the Horn of Africa Further military escalation involving Iran could also affect countries around the Horn of Africa through disruptions to maritime trade, higher fuel prices and broader diplomatic tensions. Ethiopia relies heavily on Djibouti’s ports for international trade, making the security of shipping routes through the Gulf of Aden and Red Sea especially important. Eritrea, Djibouti and Somalia also have direct geographical and economic interests in developments affecting maritime traffic around the Arabian Peninsula. Kulu Media previously examined these concerns in its coverage of the Red Sea crisis . The wider regional confrontation has also prompted governments to consider additional security measures. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi recently sought parliamentary authorization for possible defensive assistance to Saudi Arabia, although Cairo has not announced a decision to enter the conflict. The proposal was detailed in Kulu Media’s report on Egypt’s request . These developments illustrate how continued instability in the Middle East could affect security calculations across northeastern Africa. No New Military Operation Confirmed Despite Trump’s latest warning, the United States has not announced a new military operation against Iran arising from Friday’s remarks. The president did not identify a military timetable, disclose specific targets or confirm that negotiations with Tehran had ended. His comments therefore represent a warning about possible future action rather than confirmation that another attack is underway. Attention now turns to whether Washington and Tehran can make progress toward a negotiated settlement before the US midterm elections, or whether military pressure will remain central to the administration’s approach. Published 2 days ago on October 21, 2026 By Kulu Media News Desk Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh addresses the United Nations General Assembly in New York. (File photo: UN Photo) Eritrea has denied deploying troops inside Ethiopia and rejected international calls for both countries to exercise restraint, accusing the Ethiopian government of fueling regional instability amid escalating military and diplomatic tensions in the Horn of Africa. In a formal statement issued on October 21, 2026, Eritrea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said its military forces remain entirely within the country’s internationally recognized borders and described Ethiopian allegations of an invasion as fabricated. The official statement , published by Eritrea’s Ministry of Information, presents Asmara’s position on the growing confrontation, including disputed borders, military deployments, territorial sovereignty and international diplomatic efforts. The ministry insisted that Eritrea has no territorial ambitions against Ethiopia and maintains a defensive military posture. The claims could not be independently verified. Eritrea Rejects Ethiopian Allegations The Eritrean government accused Ethiopia’s ruling Prosperity Party of pursuing policies that threaten regional stability, alleging that Addis Ababa has engaged in military pressure, diplomatic hostility and efforts to undermine Eritrean sovereignty. The statement rejected allegations that Eritrean forces had invaded Ethiopia or continued operating inside Ethiopian territory. It also disputed claims concerning areas covered by the 2002 Eritrea-Ethiopia Boundary Commission decision, arguing that some accusations of Eritrean military presence refer to territory awarded to Eritrea under that ruling. The competing territorial interpretations remain a central source of disagreement between the neighboring countries. Ethiopia has previously accused Eritrea of conducting military incursions and supporting armed opposition groups, allegations that Asmara denies. The latest Eritrean statement does not independently establish the location of forces operating near the border. Asmara Challenges International Calls for Restraint In a notable diplomatic position, Eritrea criticized international appeals urging both Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate tensions. The ministry argued that calls directed equally at both governments overlook what it describes as Ethiopia’s responsibility for the confrontation. According to Asmara, diplomatic initiatives should focus on ending policies it considers threatening to Eritrean sovereignty rather than treating the two countries as equally responsible for the crisis. The position comes as international concern grows over the possibility of renewed conflict between the neighboring states. The United States and United Kingdom have called for restraint and diplomatic engagement. As previously detailed in Kulu Media’s coverage, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged de-escalation during discussions with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. The United Kingdom has also backed African Union mediation as regional tensions intensify. Sovereignty and Red Sea Dispute Eritrea’s statement also addressed the broader disagreement surrounding Ethiopia’s ambitions for access to the Red Sea. The ministry emphasized that Eritrean sovereignty and territorial integrity are non-negotiable, rejecting any attempt to justify territorial changes on economic or strategic grounds. Ethiopia, a landlocked country, has repeatedly emphasized the importance of securing reliable maritime access for its growing population and economy. However, disputes over the means of obtaining such access have contributed to deteriorating relations with Eritrea. Asmara maintained that it has no claims over Ethiopian territory and is committed to respecting internationally recognized boundaries. The ministry nevertheless warned that Eritrea remains prepared to defend its sovereignty against aggression. Growing Risk of Regional Conflict The latest statement follows weeks of deteriorating relations between Ethiopia and Eritrea, including diplomatic expulsions, accusations of military incursions and renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia. On October 1, Ethiopia announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara and the expulsion of Eritrean diplomats. Eritrea subsequently severed diplomatic relations with Ethiopia. The diplomatic breakdown has coincided with renewed military operations in Tigray, where Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have advanced through several areas previously controlled by TPLF-aligned forces. The confrontation has raised concerns about the possibility of a wider conflict involving the two countries. Kulu Media previously examined the growing war risk as military movements and competing accusations increased tensions near the border. In its October 21 statement, Eritrea maintained that sustainable regional peace requires respect for sovereignty, non-interference and internationally recognized boundaries. The government also rejected suggestions that it seeks a confrontation with Ethiopia. Despite the latest declaration, the central disagreements between Addis Ababa and Asmara remain unresolved. The immediate significance of the statement lies in Eritrea’s formal rejection of Ethiopia’s military allegations and its criticism of international diplomatic efforts that call on both governments to exercise restraint. With tensions already affecting Tigray and raising concerns across the Horn of Africa, the competing positions highlight the challenges facing efforts to prevent another major regional conflict. somalia.summary: British MP Rupert Lowe has announced a controversial plan to completely end immigration to the UK from several developing countries, including Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Somalia, and Iran. Speaking at the Restore Britain party conference on October 3, 2026, Lowe stated, “Immigration into Britain from the Third World will end entirely,” emphasizing a strict policy to halt civilian immigration from these nations. His proposals include deporting undocumented migrants, removing foreign nationals who do not meet stringent requirements, abolishing the refugee system, and tightening British citizenship rules. Lowe, who has represented Great Yarmouth since July 2024, has become a prominent figure in the UK’s hardline immigration debate, advocating for measures that extend beyond merely reducing net migration. He criticized the current immigration system as ineffective and corrupt, asserting that his party aims to implement a “red list” to discriminate against certain nationalities. This approach marks a significant shift from the UK's existing immigration framework, which allows various forms of entry for foreign nationals.

(AFP) MOGADISHU: Forces loyal to an ousted regional leader captured several key towns in southern Somalia, officials and eyewitnesses said Saturday, dealing a significant blow to the federally-backed local government. Several states in the deeply fragmented country are opposed to control by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, and in March his government sent in troops to oust the head of South West State, Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen. advertisements Since then Laftagareen has repeatedly attempted to retake the region and its main city of Baidoa. On Saturday, military officials said his forces had taken the towns of Berdale, Dinsoor, Buurhakaba, and Qansaxdheere, as well as Awdiinle town — roughly 30 kilometers (18 miles) from Baidoa — leaving the local government and allies without control of the majority of the state. “The districts currently held by Laftagareen’s forces will be brought back under government control,” South West Information Minister Nur Sidow Baba told a press conference in Baidoa. Meanwhile, in a statement, Laftagareen commended the forces loyal to him on having “successfully recaptured and liberated four districts.” The rapid changes in control — while mostly conflict-free, although clashes were reported during the takeover of Buurhakaba — have left residents worried. “In Berdale, Darawish forces loyal to Laftagareen arrived on motorcycles, heavily armed, and took control without resistance,” resident Suleyman Nurow said. He said local officials fled to a nearby base hosting the African Union mission (AUSSOM) fighting Islamist group Al-Shabab, adding that Ethiopian troops remained inside and did not intervene. “We are confused by what is happening,” Dinsoor resident Adow Yusuf said, noting that forces allied to Laftagareen appeared to now be concentrating their efforts on towns surrounding Baidoa. “They have seized several districts in a short time, encountering resistance in only one,” he added. somalia.summary: Kenya's Ministry of Health has reported significant progress in managing the Ebola outbreak, with no new cases confirmed for 17 days. The total confirmed cases remain at nine, all linked to a single cluster, and all 135 contacts have been traced, with the first group of quarantined individuals set to return home soon. The Ministry's Director General, Dr. Patrick Amoth, emphasized the effectiveness of Kenya's containment measures, which have prevented community transmission. This progress is crucial for Somalia, as Nairobi serves as a key transit hub for the region. Somalia's preparedness, however, remains a concern, with its airport screening rated at only 20% capacity and lacking dedicated isolation facilities. While Kenya has established a National Ebola Taskforce to coordinate its response, Somalia is still developing its capacity to manage potential outbreaks. The ongoing Ebola crisis in the Democratic Republic of Congo adds urgency to Somalia's efforts to strengthen its health infrastructure and response capabilities.

Editorial Featured politics SOMALIA Northeastern State: Somalia’s Cornered Frontline Region in the Red Sea Proxy Contest. Last updated: October 23, 2026 3:23 pm Pan African Visions Share SHARE Dr. Abdijalil Hassan* MOGADISHU — A geopolitical map displayed by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an October 18 security briefing has thrust Somalia’s newly inaugurated Northeastern State into the center of a widening Red Sea proxy contest, revealing a stark strategic divide between the fledgling federal member state and the UAE and Israel-aligned regions of Somaliland and Puntland. The map, which Netanyahu presented while outlining Israel’s updated national security doctrine ahead of elections, color-codes Somaliland and Puntland in light blue as part of a purported “Hexagon Alliance” friendly to Israel and the United Arab Emirates. The rest of Somalia, including the separately identified Northeastern State appears in light green under the “Sunni Diamond” grouping, comprising Türkiye, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. While the graphic was originally produced by researchers at Germany’s Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung and represents an analytical assessment of alignments rather than formal treaty commitments, its display by Netanyahu has given it unmistakable political weight. For the Northeastern State, the classification is both a strategic confirmation and a vulnerability. Inaugurated in January 2026 with the backing of the Somali federal government, the state, centered on Las Anod was created from territory previously claimed by Somaliland and Puntland, both of which have rejected the new administration and its federal alignment. the Northeastern State’s forces defeated their adversaries in late fighting and took control of contested areas that its neighbors have long claimed. That battlefield outcome has strengthened popular backing for the new federal member state among residents who view it as a long-overdue institutional answer to decades of instability and overlapping claims. the State now finds itself geographically cornered between two regions that are not only hostile to its existence but are now explicitly linked on Netanyahu’s map to the Israel-UAE strategic orbit. The map’s implications extend beyond symbolism. Somaliland has received significant diplomatic and security backing from both the UAE and Israel, particularly following Israel’s December 2025 recognition of Somaliland as an “independent state”, a move Somali Federal Republic rejected as a violation of its sovereignty. Puntland, though still a federal member state, has developed deep economic and security ties with the UAE, including involvement in the operation of Bosaso port and cooperation in military training. Together, the two regions form a de facto corridor of Emirati and Israeli influence along the Gulf of Aden, directly abutting the Northeastern State’s territory. By contrast, the Northeastern State is firmly anchored in the Sunni Diamond camp. Its federal patrons Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan have moved decisively to institutionalize their security relationship with Somalia. In August 2026, the three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, committing to collective deterrence in which an armed attack against one would be treated as an attack against all. Somalia’s defense ministry welcomed the pact as a strategic partnership capable of addressing shared security challenges. Pakistan has separately deepened defense cooperation with Mogadishu, including discussions on rebuilding the Somali Air Force and reported interest in JF-17 fighter aircraft, while Saudi Arabia signed a military cooperation memorandum with Somalia in February 2026. Egypt and Qatar have also been identified as federal allies supporting the Northeastern State’s inauguration as a counterweight to Emirati influence. Yet the presence of powerful patrons does not erase the Northeastern State’s immediate predicament. It is a new, institutionally fragile administration surrounded by rivals with established foreign backers, and its adversaries have shown no inclination to accept its legitimacy. Somaliland’s leadership has framed the state’s creation as a partition of its claimed territory; Puntland has withdrawn its recognition of the federal government altogether and joined an anti-Mogadishu political coalition. The map Netanyahu displayed did not create these tensions, but it has clarified the lines along which they are likely to escalate: the Northeastern State is not merely a domestic federal experiment but a frontline node in the competition between the Israel-UAE axis and the Türkiye-Saudi-Pakistan constellation. For the Northeastern State’s allies, the message is urgent. The state’s survival depends on tangible support, security guarantees, reconstruction funding, and diplomatic cover from Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, whose own strategic interests in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden increasingly converge on preventing the further expansion of Emirati and Israeli influence along Somalia’s northern coast. The Mecca defense pact provides a framework, but frameworks alone do not secure borders. If the Sunni Diamond powers intend to hold the line in northern Somalia, the cornered Northeastern State will need more than a color on a map. *Dr. Abdijalil Hassan ia a former lecturer at East Africa University, provides expert analysis on conflict dynamics across the Horn of Africa. Dowladda Federaalka Galmudug Hiiraan News Jubaland News Koonfur Galbeed SSC Somaliland Follow us Search News Somalia Somalia faces risk of mass displacement as floods threaten hundreds of thousands Posted by: Horseed Staff About 874,000 people in Somalia could be forced from their homes over the next three months as heavy rainfall and rising river levels increase the risk of widespread flooding, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has warned. 23 October, 2026 Share Tweet The warning comes as communities across the country continue to recover from prolonged drought and repeated displacement. The IOM said on Wednesday that the risk of flooding between October and December could leave hundreds of thousands of people without homes or livelihoods. The situation is being compounded by forecasts of above-average rainfall, as El Niño conditions are expected to intensify. “We are looking at the possibility of hundreds of thousands of people losing their homes in just a matter of weeks,” said Manuel Marques Pereira, the IOM’s chief of mission in Somalia. “Many of these families have already been displaced before and have very little left to fall back on.” Mr Marques Pereira said there was still an opportunity to reduce the impact of the floods, but warned that time was running out. “We urgently need funding to help people protect their homes and livelihoods, reach safer ground where necessary, and avoid another cycle of displacement,” he said. The warning has raised concerns over the prospect of people being forced to undertake dangerous journeys in search of safety, including across borders and by sea. Humanitarian organisations have also warned that climate-related disasters could further deepen Somalia’s existing humanitarian crisis, with the risk of severe food shortages and famine. Somalia has faced repeated droughts, floods and displacement in recent years, placing additional pressure on communities already struggling with limited access to food, water and basic services. El Niño occurs when sea surface temperatures rise in parts of the central and eastern Pacific Ocean. The phenomenon can disrupt atmospheric circulation and influence weather patterns around the world. Its effects vary from region to region. In some areas it can contribute to severe drought, while in others it can bring heavier rainfall and an increased risk of flooding. For Somalia, the immediate concern is that further flooding could force already vulnerable communities from their homes once again, adding to a cycle of displacement that humanitarian agencies are struggling to address. The meeting, held on October 23, 2026, focused on expanding cooperation in military training and improving the skills of SNA personnel. Both officials emphasized the importance of developing a professional and combat-ready national army that can effectively manage security responsibilities throughout Somalia. They also highlighted the need for ongoing support to bolster the operational capacity of the SNA. The EUTM-Somalia is part of the EU's broader initiative to assist Somalia in strengthening its security sector, which includes providing military training and advice to develop the country's security forces. This collaboration is crucial as Somalia seeks to enhance its national forces and take on greater responsibility for security operations across the nation.

تصل معركة البقاء في دوري أبطال أفريقيا "توتال إنرجيز" لموسم 2026/2027 إلى مرحلة حاسمة في عطلة نهاية هذا الأسبوع؛ إذ تواجه أندية أفريقية عريقة خطر الإقصاء المبكر، بينما تسعى فرق طموحة لتحقيق مفاجآت مدوية وحجز مقاعدها في دور المجموعات. يتعين على أندية الترجي التونسي (بطل أفريقيا أربع مرات)، ومولودية الجزائر، وبترو أتلتيكو الأنغولي، تعويض خسائرها المؤلمة في مباريات الذهاب، وذلك خلال جولة الإياب من الدور التمهيدي الثاني، التي تُقام 15 مباراة منها في الفترة ما بين الجمعة 23 أكتوبر والأحد 25 أكتوبر 2026. كما يواجه حامل اللقب، ماميلودي صنداونز، اختباراً مصيرياً بعد تعادله سلبياً في مباراة الذهاب أمام فريق "ويليتي" الأنغولي، في حين يتوجب على تي بي مازيمبي -الفائز باللقب خمس مرات- تجاوز عقبة النادي الأفريقي التونسي للحفاظ على آماله القارية. وتأتي هذه الجولة الحاسمة بعد تأهل نادي "يانغ أفريكانز" التنزاني، الذي أصبح أول فريق يضمن مقعداً في دور المجموعات، عقب فوزه يوم الأربعاء على "سي إف إف إيه" ( CFFA ) من مدغشقر بنتيجة 4-1، ليحسم المواجهة لصالحه بنتيجة إجمالية بلغت 8-1. ومع تأهل "يانغ أفريكانز" بالفعل، تتبقى 15 مقعداً شاغراً في دور المجموعات، الذي من المقرر أن ينطلق في أواخر شهر نوفمبر. ومن بين أكثر المواجهات إثارة، يسعى الترجي التونسي لإنقاذ مسيرته في البطولة عندما يستضيف فريق "السويحلي" الليبي يوم السبت؛ حيث يمتلك الفريق الليبي أفضلية الفوز ذهاباً بنتيجة 1-0، ولا يفصله سوى 90 دقيقة عن تحقيق أحد أكبر الإنجازات في تاريخه القاري. وفي مواجهة صعبة أخرى، يستقبل مولودية الجزائر فريق "رينجرز إنترناشيونال" النيجيري يوم الجمعة، وهو مطالب بتعويض خسارته ذهاباً بهدفين نظيفين. وفي سياق مشابه، يواجه بترو أتلتيكو الأنغولي تحدياً كبيراً عند استضافته لفريق "سكوتلاند إف سي" الزيمبابوي، بعد أن انتهت مباراة الذهاب بخسارة الفريق الأنغولي بهدفين دون رد. يواجه فريق "صنداونز" اختباراً صعباً عندما يستضيف "ويليتي" في بريتوريا، وذلك بعد أن انتهت مباراة الذهاب في أنغولا بالتعادل السلبي (0-0). وفي تونس، تُقام مواجهة قوية أخرى يوم الأحد، حيث يستضيف "النادي الأفريقي" فريق "تي ​​بي مازيمبي" -الفائز باللقب الأفريقي خمس مرات- بعد أن تعادل الفريقان بنتيجة (1-1) في لوبومباشي. وبينما تواجه بعض الأندية العريقة ضغوطاً كبيرة، تسعى أندية أخرى لحسم تأهلها رسمياً بعد تقديمها أداءً قوياً في مباريات الذهاب. يدخل فريق "نهضة بركان" المغربي مباراة الإياب على أرضه يوم السبت متسلحاً بتقدمه (2-0) على "ستار سبورت أكاديمي" من سيراليون، بينما يسعى "الهلال" السوداني للحفاظ على تقدمه بنفس النتيجة أمام "بن سيداما " الإثيوبي يوم الأحد. كما يتمتع فريق "كولومب سبورتيف" الكاميروني بوضع مريح بعد تحقيقه فوزاً لافتاً خارج أرضه بنتيجة (2-0) على "تونغيث" السنغالي، مما يجعله على أعتاب التأهل لدور المجموعات. وقد تشهد المرحلة المقبلة حضوراً مزدوجاً لتنزانيا؛ إذ يُعد فريق "سيمبا" الأقرب للانضمام إلى "يانغ أفريكانز" بعد تحقيقه فوزاً ساحقاً بنتيجة (6-1) خارج دياره على "15 دي أغوستو" من غينيا الاستوائية يوم الأربعاء. وفي مصر، يسعى كل من "بيراميدز" و"الزمالك" لحسم التأهل على أرضهما يوم السبت، بعد أن حقق كلاهما الفوز بنتيجة (1-0) خارج الديار في جولة الذهاب، أمام "المريخ بنتيو" من جنوب السودان و"الجيش" الرواندي على التوالي. ويضع فريق "أورلاندو بايرتس" الجنوب أفريقي نفسه في موقف جيد بعد فوزه (1-0) خارج ملعبه على "أفريكان ستارز" الناميبي، رغم أنه سيحتاج إلى تقديم أداء منضبط مجدداً في مباراة الإياب. وفي سياق آخر، يأمل فريق "أسيك ميموزا" الإيفواري في استغلال عاملي الأرض والجمهور أمام "المغرب الفاسي" المغربي، بعد تعادلهما (1-1) في لقاء الذهاب. أما فريق "هورويا" الغيني فيسافر لمواجهة "المريخ" السوداني وهو متقدم بفارق ضئيل (1-0)، في حين يتعين على "نواذيبو" الموريتاني تعويض خسارته ذهاباً (2-1) أمام "سان بيدرو" الإيفواري. تشير الفوارق الضئيلة في العديد من هذه المواجهات إلى أن نتائج معارك التأهل لا تزال غير محسومة، مع احتمالية حدوث المزيد من المفاجآت في ظل سعي الأندية المستمر للبقاء في دائرة المنافسة على المجد القاري. وستنضم الأندية الـ 15 المتأهلة إلى فريق "يانغ أفريكانز" في دور المجموعات، الذي يضم 16 فريقاً، ضمن منافسات دوري أبطال أفريقيا "توتال إنرجيز" لموسم 2026/2027. دوري أبطال
